title: Give credit for a biology finding
objective: Name the source of a fact and describe how you used AI.

slides.title: Whose words and whose finding?
body: Put copied words in quotation marks. Name the source.
When you tell the idea in your own words, the finding still needs its source.
If you used AI, check the facts against the source and follow your course rules.

slides.title: Keep track of the source
body: A class note by Lek says, “We saw four ants on the leaf.”
Possible report: Lek recorded four ants on a leaf.
If AI helped with spelling, say exactly that. Never supply a reference you have not checked.

slides.title: Read the first case together
body: Classroom source: Field Note A, by Mali. “We counted ten snails near the pond.” You used an AI tool to check spelling only.

slides.title: Try it with a partner
body: Write the finding in your own words and name the source.
Explain why a student should name the source.

slides.title: Try a new case
body: Classroom source: Field Note B, by Niran. “We saw six birds in the garden.” You used an AI tool to check spelling only.

slides.title: Work on your own
body: Write the finding in your own words and name the source.
Explain why a student should name the source.
Write one honest sentence about your AI use.

slides.title: Check the source trail
body: Can a reader find the person or text behind the number? Can the reader tell what AI did?
